reason: The text contains several named characters who are not leaders. Most notably, Eve (Chavah/חַוָּה) is explicitly named in Genesis 3:20 but is not portrayed as a leader—she is deceived by the serpent and eats the forbidden fruit, and is subsequently told that her husband will have dominion over her. The serpent (ha-nachash/הַנָּחָשׁ) is a character in the narrative but is not a leader; rather, it is an adversary/tempter. While God (YHWH/Elohim) is unambiguously a leader with ultimate authority and Adam has some delegated authority (naming the animals, dominion over creation), the presence of Eve as an explicitly named character who is not a leader invalidates the statement.
